source:
Backyard Monsters is one of the most underappreciated strategy games ever made. It combined Clash of Clans, Factorio, tower defense, RTS, and idle progression years before most mobile games. The core loop was: build a monster base, gather resources, research new monsters, attack other players, and defend your own base while upgrades continued in real time.
I actually think a Roblox spiritual successor could be bigger than the original, because Roblox solves many of the social and multiplayer limitations that Facebook games had.

The Fantasy
You're not building a town.
You're growing a monster civilization hidden inside a suburban backyard.
Imagine:
 • gigantic mushrooms
 • monster nests
 • slime rivers
 • tree forts
 • toy blocks
 • abandoned bicycles
 • sprinklers become rivers
 • garden hoses become bridges
 • sandbox becomes a desert biome
The world feels gigantic because you're tiny.

Core Gameplay Loop

Login

↓

Collect resources

↓

Upgrade buildings

↓

Breed new monsters

↓

Scout nearby players

↓

Attack enemy bases

↓

Steal resources

↓

Expand territory

↓

Unlock stronger monsters

↓

Repeat

Every mechanic feeds this loop.

Layer 1 - Base Building
The base is your kingdom.
You start with

Monster Heart

Everything branches from it.
You place
Resource Extractors
Storages
Monster Housing
Walls
Turrets
Laboratories
Breeding Caves
Spell Towers
Decoration
Eventually
Huge Fortress

Resources
Instead of generic gold/elixir.
Make every resource thematic.
Example
Mush
Organic material.
Used for
 • buildings
 • walls

Goo
Monster food.
Used to
 • train monsters
 • breeding

Bones
Military resource.
Used for
 • advanced monsters
 • weapons

Electricity
Harvested from backyard electronics.
Used for
High-tech monsters.

Scrap
Found from
Broken toys
Soda cans
Old tools
Used for
Mechanical monsters.

Building Loop
Every building upgrades.
Level 1
Small nest.
Level 20
Massive fortress.
Visual progression matters.
Players LOVE seeing bases evolve.

Monster Collection
Instead of troops...
Think Pokémon meets Clash.
Each monster has

Role

Size

Element

Abilities

Movement

Housing Cost

Rarity

Examples
Tiny Gobbler
Fast melee.
Rock Rhino
Tank.
Spitter
Long-range acid.
Firefly
Flying DPS.
Mole
Burrows under walls.
Spider Queen
Summons babies.
Boom Beetle
Explodes.
Living Tree
Siege tank.
Dragon
Legendary.

Monster Classes

Common

Rare

Epic

Legendary

Ancient

Mythic

Not paywalled.
Obtained through
Research
Bosses
Events
Breeding
Exploration

Monster Progression
Each monster has
Level
Mastery
Mutations
Traits
Example
Fire Beetle
Level 1
↓
Level 20
↓
Mutation
Now explodes.
Later
Mutation
Leaves lava.

Research Tree
One of the best parts of Backyard Monsters.
Huge tech tree.
Example

Military

├── Faster monsters

├── Better AI

├── Larger armies

└── Flying units

Defense

├── Walls

├── Cannons

├── Traps

└── Shields

Economy

├── Storage

├── Mining

├── Production

└── Automation

Magic

├── Spells

├── Summons

├── Weather

└── Rituals

Research takes
Minutes
Hours
Days

Army Building
Instead of
"train 50 troops"
Players create squads.
Example
Squad Alpha
Tank
Tank
Healer
Healer
DPS
DPS
Flying
Flying
Each squad has a strategy.

Battle Gameplay
Here's where I'd improve massively.
Old Backyard Monsters was mostly click-and-watch.
Instead...
Hybrid RTS.
Player
Drops monsters.
Can
Ping targets.
Cast spells.
Retreat.
Use abilities.
Activate ultimate.
Enough control to feel involved.
Not enough to overwhelm.

Base Defense
Every base should feel unique.
Defenses include
Spike traps
Acid pools
Tesla towers
Slime launchers
Monster dens
Poison flowers
Giant Venus flytraps
Rocket squirrels
Laser garden gnomes
Everything fits the backyard theme.

Terrain Matters
Huge improvement.
Height matters.
Trees block vision.
Water slows.
Mud traps.
Sprinklers flood.
Tall grass hides units.
Sandbox slows heavy monsters.
Terrain creates strategy.

AI Behavior
Instead of dumb pathfinding.
Each monster has priorities.
Tank

Attack nearest defense

Protect allies

Taunt

Assassin

Ignore walls

Jump inside

Kill defenses

Escape

Healer

Stay behind

Heal lowest HP

Retreat

Makes every monster feel alive.

Exploration
The original mostly stayed around PvP.
I'd add PvE.
Outside your base
Procedurally generated backyard.
Find
Abandoned toys
Insect nests
Bird houses
Storm drains
Garages
Treehouses
Each biome contains
Resources
Bosses
Secrets
Rare monsters

World Map
Think
Backyard
↓
Neighborhood
↓
City Park
↓
Sewer
↓
School Playground
↓
Construction Site
↓
Shopping Center
↓
National Forest
World continually expands.

Bosses
Huge creatures.
Garden Snake
Lawn Mower
Cat
Dog
Crow
Spider Queen
Raccoon
Each drops
Unique monster DNA.

Breeding System
One of the biggest missing opportunities.
Example
Fire Beetle
 • 
Rock Rhino
↓
Lava Rhino
Players experiment.
Hundreds of combinations.
Like DragonVale meets Pokémon.

Seasons
Weather affects gameplay.
Rain
More Goo.
Winter
Frozen rivers.
Summer
Fire monsters stronger.
Autumn
Leaf camouflage.

Alliances
Neighborhood Monster Clubs.
Members
Donate monsters.
Share resources.
Raid bosses.
Alliance wars.
Alliance tech tree.
Alliance fortress.

PvP
Three modes.
Raid
Steal resources.
Ranked
Lose/gain trophies.
War
Alliance vs Alliance.

Reputation
Instead of trophies only.
Neighborhood Reputation.
Higher reputation unlocks
NPC traders.
Legendary bosses.
Special cosmetics.
Elite players.

Endgame
Not just bigger numbers.
Players chase
Monster encyclopedia completion
Perfect mutations
Rare decorations
Alliance rankings
Seasonal leaderboards
World bosses
Legendary base skins

Live Events
Weekly
Meteor crashes.
Alien invasion.
Backyard flooded.
Neighborhood barbecue.
Halloween monsters.
Christmas toy factory.
Every event changes gameplay.

Idle Progression
Offline
Resources continue.
Research continues.
Breeding continues.
Monster healing continues.
Expeditions continue.
Enough idle to respect players' time, but not so much that active play feels unnecessary.

Roblox-Specific Improvements
This is where a clone can become something much larger.
Instead of every player living in an isolated instance, imagine an entire persistent neighborhood server with 20-40 players.
Each player owns one backyard, but everyone can:
 • Walk to neighboring yards.
 • Watch live attacks.
 • Trade monster DNA.
 • Visit alliance fortresses.
 • Participate in neighborhood events (like defending against a giant cat invading multiple bases).
This makes the world feel alive in a way the original never could.

Technical Architecture

Server
├── Persistent World
├── Base Simulation
├── Resource Production
├── Combat Engine
├── Pathfinding
├── AI Behavior Trees
├── Research System
├── Alliance System
├── Matchmaking
├── Economy
└── Live Events

Client
├── Building Mode
├── RTS Controls
├── Combat VFX
├── Monster Animation
├── UI
├── Camera
└── Audio

Each player's base is an independently simulated "island" within the larger neighborhood, allowing efficient server performance while still supporting social interactions and live events.

Long-Term Retention
The best strategy games always have goals on multiple timescales:
 • 5-minute session: Collect resources, queue upgrades, check breeding results, attack one nearby base.
 • 30-minute session: Explore a new biome, defeat a boss, redesign your defenses, experiment with a new army composition.
 • Weekly goal: Complete alliance events, unlock a new monster family, climb ranked PvP, finish research branches.
 • Monthly goal: Earn limited seasonal monsters, evolve Ancient monsters, upgrade your fortress, and compete for neighborhood dominance.
The original Backyard Monsters proved that combining base building, asynchronous PvP, and long-term progression was compelling. A modern Roblox version could push that much further by emphasizing collectible monsters with unique AI, exploration beyond the home base, cooperative neighborhood gameplay, and a living world that changes through seasonal events rather than simply recreating the original formula.

answers.ask: Should we build one backyard base first, or the whole neighbourhood world map? Eight expanding world tiers will not fit in a single top-down image, so they would be separate maps.
answers.answer: Build one backyard base first as the playable vertical slice. The wider world map and its expanding tiers can come later as separate maps.

answers.ask: Are the neighbouring players' yards inside the same map as yours, or separate instances you travel to?
answers.answer: Neighbouring players' yards should be separate instances you travel to for scouting and raids, keeping each base focused and readable.

Center the layout on a Monster Heart, with clear buildable territory branching outward for monster nests and housing, resource extractors and storages, laboratories, breeding caves, spell towers, defensive walls, turrets, traps, acid pools, slime launchers, poison flowers, Venus flytraps, and a future fortress footprint. Surround the base with oversized backyard terrain and landmarks: gigantic mushrooms, tall grass, trees and tree forts, slime rivers, a sprinkler-fed water channel, garden-hose bridges, toy blocks, abandoned bicycles, broken toys, soda cans, old tools, and a sandbox forming a small desert biome. Use height changes, mud, water, cover-providing trees and grass, and open approach routes to shape the terrain. Keep this yard as a focused standalone base map; neighboring player yards are separate destinations rather than visible plots in the same scene.

## Genre

The dominant genre is Strategy, with Simulation secondary for the persistent building, extraction, and upgrade loop.

## Shape and preset

Use `terrain-open`: units move dynamically across one backyard rather than following a hard-coded lane. Match the Real-Time Strategy preset, retaining its open terrain and core/base-building options while adapting it to one defensible player base.

## Config requirements

Draw `buildzone-plot` as broad buildable territory radiating from the Monster Heart. Draw the visible `tracker-core` as that central heart. Add `terrain-relief` through modest backyard height changes without overhangs, and `water-body` as slime rivers plus the sprinkler-fed channel. Include open attack approaches, walls, turrets, traps, acid pools, slime launchers, poison flowers, Venus flytraps, nests, housing, extractors, storages, laboratories, breeding caves, spell towers, and a reserved fortress footprint. Oversized mushrooms, grass, trees, tree forts, hose bridges, toys, bicycle, cans, tools, and the sandbox establish tiny-creature scale.

## Layout requirements

Bind the functional `tracker-core` to the single Monster Heart at map center. Place `collectible-nodes` as thematic Mush, Goo, Bones, Electricity, and Scrap sites near matching backyard materials, outside the innermost defenses but reachable from build territory. No neighboring-yard placement belongs in this map.

## Layout components

Center one base core and fan buildable sectors around it. Ring these with defensive structures while preserving several open perimeter-to-core approaches. Put the sandbox desert on one edge, wet slime and sprinkler channels across another, and hose bridges at crossings. Use raised dry ground for long-range defenses, mud and water in low ground, and trees or tall grass as sight blockers. The yard boundary encloses the standalone scene. Compose it as a readable 3D top-down base plan.

## Render order

Render `topdown` first and treat it as authoritative, then dress the isometric view, because build sectors, approaches, resource access, and defensive sightlines must remain tactically legible.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost

Scale is large for one complete backyard base. The theme is whimsical monster civilization amid colossal suburban debris. Route `tiered` for non-overhanging height changes and `CHECK` for playable water channels; no `P4` applies because other yards are deferred destinations, not maps in this build.
